reviews.title: Basic Motherboard with Good Features
reviews.comment:
Bought a few times for budget and mid range computer builds and they never failed me after several months of use.
Pro 1: Q-Flash! Why don’t all manufacturers make their own for all boards? The ability to flash the BIOS with just the PSU and a USB drive.
Pro 2: The features on this board. Q-Flash. No screw NVMe latch. ARGB headers. Full CPU support. Some boards in this price range only support 65 watt or less CPU’s.
Pro Tip: This is a budget board. You will degrade the board in time with overclocking.
Would I buy it again? Yes.
reviews.author: Amazon_Shopper

reviews.title: DOA, buyer beware
reviews.comment: Purchased this as the lowest price option for a home theater build. No frills or anything, simple 1 stick of RAM and M.2 build. Would not POST. DRAM LED right off the rip. Reset CMOS, tested components separately, checked with known good RAM sticks and simply will not progress. Left the unit running for about an hour just to see if some strange memory learning thing was ongoing as AMD will sometimes do. Simply dead. Return process initiated and now back on the search for another low priced AM5 board in mATX.
reviews.author: M Jordan

reviews.title: Does What I Needed
reviews.comment: This is a cheap motherboard, so I'm not going to pretend it's amazing, but it works well and I've had no problems with it. The Q-Flash was a life saver since the processor I bought wasn't compatible with the installed BIOS. I'd recommend for anyone on a budget.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wesley Openshaw

reviews.title: Heads up 8500G, 8600G, 8700G, 8000 series Ryzen CPU
reviews.comment:
This is important information because Gigabyte has completely useless customer service and lacks the foresight to put any pertinent information on their website.
If you're buying this motherboard to use with your 8000 series Ryzen processor, it does not come with the right BIOS installed, you have to get an 8-16GB USB 2.0 thumb drive, format it to FAT32, and download either the F20 or the F30 drivers from their website(or any of the drivers in between)
And THEN, you have to unzip the folder into the usb 2.0 drive and rename the A620MS2H.F30 to gigabyte.bin (This is really important, it just won't work unless you do this and I don't know why this isn't in the readme.)
And THEN you have to connect the 8 pin and the 20 pin to the board (you can do it with the board populated or bare, it really doesn't matter as long as the board has power) and then you put the USB 2.0 drive into the slot marked "BIOS" you might need to check the orientation to find it,
and THEN you hit the Q Flash Plus button and wait for the entire thing to stop blinking, it takes 5-6 minutes.
You should be able to get it working with these instructions. OR, you can spend an entire week in an email loop with Gigabyte's customer service as they walk you in circles.
reviews.author: Joe
